verdicts.reason: The card's only differentiator, 'compliant memory', is something every reseller of Samsung, SK hynix, Micron or Kingston product already meets at no cost. It loses on price and access and only ties on compliance and small-business status, so it wins no axis. Whatever §5949 creates that buyers would pay for is verification (C-64), not resale margin.

verdicts.reason: The card concedes that IP without a line is worthless. The only XPoint line (Lehi) went to TI in 2021 for $900M cash plus ~$600M of tools and now runs analog. Micron quit, citing 'insufficient market validation' after ~$545M of underutilization charges, and Intel lost >$7B. Any product path therefore needs a new 20nm-class crosspoint PCM fab, which is >$1B (T4, A-11). The licensing-only path fails on its premise. A 2026 search found no revival or licensing activity. At the canonical $6.40/GB glut the cost gap that sank Optane closes again.
